At the audit (pass 3, 1993) the assessor listed these remediation items, quoted:
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:1049-1095 — the regenerated head on the wide, un-remodelled cut surface is a localised spot (CV_theta = 0.95) and the model regenerates head before ring (t_head = 450 < t_ring = 1050), contrary to Meinhardt's (1993) tentacle-first prediction. Add wound closure (taper the fragment tip radius over time) and a tentacle gating that does not require sigma to rise under the new head, then test the regeneration order explicitly.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:1146-1166 and 1740 — the body-length sweep count skips 6 (5 -> 7) and all shell results come from a single seed; report tentacle count and ring offset across >= 5 seeds and a finer L grid so the specimen's 6 is bracketed with an uncertainty, not a single run.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:169-172 — the reference JSON is hashed at runtime but not pinned in EXPECTED_SHA256, so the parity block can drift silently; pin it (update the digest when the JSON changes) and have measure_outputs report a mismatch.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:1744-1783 — four new measurements use model-internal reference values ((L-1)/L for the foot, the default run's own leak for the ablation, 1.0 for the Spearman and recovery metrics). Replace them with literature values (e.g. foot/peduncle position and tentacle number vs body size from a Hydra size series) or label them explicitly as internal consistency checks in the measurement names.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:695-785 — specimen references depend on hand-set thresholds (tissue fraction 0.98, +0.5 px distance tolerance, 28 deg basal sector) measured on one obliquely photographed polyp; report their sensitivity (vary the thresholds, add a second CC-licensed specimen) and propagate the resulting band widths into the shell measurements.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:788-799 and 913-923 — THREE_SYSTEM_PARAMS and the coupling functions tentacle_drive / foot_drive are this implementation's reduced forms (Hill gating sigma^8/(0.6^8+sigma^8), suppression 1/(1+kappa_a a), foot 1/(1+(sigma/0.03)^2)). Digitise Meinhardt (1993) appendix equations (incl. the foot -> source-density negative feedback) and either implement them or tabulate term-by-term where the reduced form departs, with equation numbers in the docstrings and in math_kg_loops.
- remediation needed: 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py:800 and 1733-1742 — SHELL_DEFAULT_LENGTH_CELLS = 90 is a scale calibration against the specimen's spacing / body length, and the shell still yields 7 tentacles vs 6 while the 1D ring (N_ring = 64, L433-470) selects a different wavelength (10.7 vs 8.1 cells) with the same D_b, D_c. Derive one absolute scale (um per cell) from the specimen's body length and tentacle spacing, use it for BOTH the ring and the shell, and add a D_c sweep on the shell so the audit can see whether kinetics or geometry sets the count.

At the audit (pass 3, 1972) the assessor listed these remediation items, quoted:
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:600-603 — the K14-Wnt 'overexpression' preset changes kappa (0.02 -> 0.015), D_w (0.015 -> 0.008) and D_h (0.45 -> 0.32) together with rho_w, so the 2.0x density is a lattice-scale preset, not a WNT-overexpression perturbation. Add a pure rho_w sweep at fixed D_w/D_h/kappa (and a c_w sweep) and report how placode count, area and NN spacing respond; keep the preset only as a labelled 'compressed-scale' control.
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:678-696 and 726-768 — all dermal constants (D_f, mu_f, s_f, D_b, mu_b, s_b, D_rho, chi_f, chi_b, v_peg) are hand-tuned dimensionless values with mechanism citations but no value provenance. Pin at least fibroblast speed / DC formation time to Glover et al. (2017) live-imaging data and the FGF20 range to Huh et al. (2013), record them in the JSON with units, and derive the dimensionless groups from them.
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:771-925 (peg ODE at 847, stage thresholds at 888-891) — the dermal coupling is one-way and the hair peg is a scalar depth with ordinal stage cut-offs at 25%/50% of a 12-layer slab. Replace the scalar with an epidermal invagination field (phase-field or level-set interface driven by the DC), add DC -> epidermis feedback (DC-derived Noggin/FGF maintaining the placode), and calibrate slab depth and peg length to micrometres from Paus et al. (1999) / Huh et al. (2013) sections so the stage histogram is testable rather than conventional.
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:836 and 943 — BMP4 is produced uniformly in proportion to rho (no interfollicular-epidermal or DC-localised source) and the BMP4 axis is evaluated at a single 5x point. Add a spatially structured BMP source (interfollicular epidermis as in Mou et al. 2006) and a bmp4_scale sweep showing monotone suppression of DC count / peg depth, with a Noggin rescue control (Botchkarev 1999).
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:847, 860 and 867-876 — e_thr = 1.6 is used both as the peg-ODE onset (847) and as the DC segmentation threshold (860), and the DC-placode registration radius 2.5 px is arbitrary; the DC/placode ratio 1.0 and Fgf20-null = 0 are therefore partly by construction. Decouple detection (e.g. Otsu on the upper-dermal density) from the dynamics threshold and report sensitivity of N_DC and offset to both.
- remediation needed: 2002-sick-wnt-dkk-hair-follicle.py:974-1042 and 1570-1579 — the vendored specimen is a Gad1 in situ of vibrissa/hair placodes (Maddox & Condie 2004) and its NN-spacing CV (0.323) does not match the PDE lattice (0.086); count equality (15 vs 16) is not a meaningful specimen metric on an arbitrary 42-cell domain. Vendor a pelage-pattern image (or digitise Sick et al. 2006 Fig. 2A/2C placode centroids), compare the NN-spacing distributions scale-free (spacing/lambda, CV, KS statistic) as a first-class measurement with a pass band, and state the vibrissa image as a secondary control.
- remediation needed: docs/media/wnt_dkk_hair_follicle_comparison.png row D — no reference image (Huh 2013 Fig. 1 DC sections, Glover 2017 live-imaging aggregation, or a Paus 1999 stage panel) is shown beside the model, so the condensate shape, depth (centre of mass 0.41 layers) and peg morphology are judged against nothing; vendor a CC-licensed DC/hair-germ section and segment it as was done for Panel C1.

What the assessor says the source reports: Raspopovic et al. (2014): a 3-node network of cell-autonomous Sox9 with diffusing Bmp and Wnt (Sox9 represses both ligands, Bmp activates and Wnt represses Sox9) is Turing-unstable without ligand self-activation; Sox9 digit stripes are out of phase with Bmp and Wnt; on the growing autopod a distal FGF / Hoxd gradient that lengthens the wavelength keeps the stripes unbranched, and the growing-domain simulations were run on a realistic limb-bud growth map (Marcon et al. 2011) | Sheth et al. (2012): digit number scales with autopod width / Hox dosage through the Turing wavelength | Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999): on a growing domain every species acquires the dilution term -(div u) c and modes are inserted sequentially as the domain lengthens | Boehm et al. Report the band of admissible counts per arc (from the dispersion band sigma > 0.9 sigma_max) and tighten the test, or average over seeds.
- remediation needed: 2014-raspopovic-bmp-sox9-wnt-digits.py:1721-1812 and datasets/bmp_sox9_wnt_digits/limb_bud_outgrowth_fem_reference.json — eight of nine Pass 3 references are analytic / model-internal. Vendor measured anchors (Sheth 2012 width vs digit number, Raspopovic Fig. 4 stripe counts with and without modulation) and compare the FEM ray width, spacing CV and taper with the segmented specimen rays.
- remediation needed: 2014-raspopovic-bmp-sox9-wnt-digits.py:303-365 (L318 d_scale = (k_bs_eff / k_bs)^3.12 * fgf_scale^2) with datasets/bmp_sox9_wnt_digits/bmp_sox9_wnt_digits_reference.json `fgf_hox_wavelength_scaling` — the 7-regime wavelength collapse is produced by a fitted exponent; with D fixed the network shortens lambda_c as k_bs rises (5.02 -> 3.27 for k_bs 1.0 -> 3.2). Retrieve the Raspopovic et al. (2014) supplementary modulation functions, re-derive which parameter the FGF / Hox gradients modulate, and re-score the table without a fitted exponent.
- remediation needed: 2014-raspopovic-bmp-sox9-wnt-digits.py:476-594 (L526-528 mode seeding, L549-550 radial diffusion x 0.0008, L514 / L560-567 cosmetic envelope) — the v2 2D polar-fan solver imposes its 5-ray result. At the audit (pass 3, 2000) the assessor listed these remediation items, quoted:
- remediation needed: 2020-bailleul-allometric-cranial-sutures.py:322-344 and 386-389 with datasets/allometric_cranial_sutures/allometric_cranial_sutures_reference.json:135-180 — the vault strain is Gaussian deflection Hessians plus an isotropic ICP term; it fails the lambdoid > sagittal SII comparison (0.885 vs 1.22) for every nuchal scale in the sweep. Implement a thin-shell (Koiter/Kirchhoff-Love) finite-difference or FEM solve with membrane equilibrium on the ellipsoid (or vendor an open CT skull mesh) and re-run the three-suture comparison.
- remediation needed: 2020-bailleul-allometric-cranial-sutures.py:466-491 — `construct_osteogenic_front_curve` normalises the KS field by std(h) (L471, L479, L483) and adds hand-coded cascade harmonics (0.62/0.34/0.16) and a lobe drive, so D_f and SII are set by the construction rather than by the PDE amplitude. Replace with a solved bidirectional interface (Zollikofer & Weissmann 2011 two-front growth or a 2D phase-field level set) whose overhang emerges from normal growth, and let the KS amplitude propagate.
- remediation needed: 2020-bailleul-allometric-cranial-sutures.py:762-768 and 851-853 — Spearman correlations use a ties-unaware argsort-of-argsort, which is why the depth profile reports -0.90 rather than -1.0 for a monotone profile with two saturated layers. Use `scipy.stats.spearmanr` and add a tie-aware monotonicity test.
- remediation needed: 2020-bailleul-allometric-cranial-sutures.py:893-913 — only the sagittal suture is extractable from the vendored photograph. Vendor a CC-licensed lateral/posterior view (coronal + lambdoid in frame) and an endocranial view, extend `segment_human_suture_specimen` to arbitrary oriented ROIs, and turn measurements 7-8 into specimen comparisons instead of null/vendored references.
- remediation needed: datasets/allometric_cranial_sutures/allometric_cranial_sutures_reference.json:151 and 2020-bailleul-allometric-cranial-sutures.py:616-631 — the explicit -alpha_dev(x) h_xx term needs an alpha clip of 3.0 for stability and the clip changes the lambdoid mean alpha (2.0 -> 1.06, 3.0 -> 1.27). Treat the heterogeneous term implicitly (IMEX / Crank-Nicolson on alpha(x) k^2) so no clip is required, and report the lambdoid profile unclipped.

What the assessor says the source reports: Goriely & Tabor (1998) / McMillen & Goriely (2002): an intrinsically curved Kirchhoff rod with both ends held undergoes a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation below T_c = B kappa_0^2 / (1 + Gamma) into two opposite-handed helices joined by a perversion, with zero net link | Gerbode et al. (2012): the cucumber tendril's G-fiber ribbon sets the intrinsic curvature; soft tendrils (Gamma < 1) overwind under axial stretch while lignified ones unwind; coil radius and pitch scale across species | Darwin (1865) Ch. IV: tendrils curve toward a touched side within tens of seconds, complete a wrap around a thin stick within minutes to about an hour, and grasp thin supports more readily than thick ones (qualitative) | Jaffe & Galston (1968): thigmotropic coiling is a contact-triggered, propagating growth response; Euler (1762): the capstan law exp(mu Theta) for a flexible line on a cylinder
limitations: Imported record of what upstream's files say. Frontier did not run upstream code and did not check the source paper's equations; the assessor is a language model working for the same author as the script, so this is not independent evidence.

Citation provenance: text taken from math_kg spec model_spec.model (the reference dataset has no matching metadata.sources entry); the audit's DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.80.1564 appears in the reference dataset text, and the script's file name (1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py) is upstream's own label.

The contact solver is a separate bending-only rod: it has no material-frame twist, so Gamma = C/B plays no role in contact coiling and the perversion (zero-link) physics of section 3 is not coupled to it | mu_support, mu_self, kappa_contact, tau_thigmo, v_signal, the 55 deg approach angle and the initial placement touching the support at 25 % of L are provenance-tagged assumptions; the only empirical anchors for Pass 3 are Darwin's qualitative timings and support-size statements | Friction uses normal forces lagged one macro step; F_hold / mu*sum(N) = 0.67 is a consistency check of the scheme, not an experiment; N_wrap counts loose loops that enclose but do not touch the support (contact fraction 33 % of nodes)

Circumnutation or support-search before first touch, a measured tendril-on-wood friction coefficient, compliant or rough or finite-length supports, G-fiber lignification time course, or a validated time-to-wrap (tau_thigmo and v_signal were chosen inside Darwin's 5-60 min window and the model's 4.75 min falls slightly below it).

At the audit (pass 3, 2002) the assessor listed these remediation items, quoted:
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:1221, 897-899 and 2051-2056 — housekeeping: the section-6 banner still says '6-Panel'; `_last_objective`, `_mat_dir`, `_last_opt_message` are unused and `last_objective` is unbound when t_end_min < dt_min; the determinism check covers only a 5 min horizon. Also morphoeval/lean/loops/Loop_064_tendril_perversion_intrinsic_curvature.lean:1-12 — the header lists only the three Pass 2 sources although Laws 4-5 cite Darwin (1865), Jaffe & Galston (1968) and Euler (1762).
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:1841-1850 and 1831-1840 — the time-to-first-wrap measurement (4.75 min vs reference 32.5 min) is set by the assumed tau_thigmo = 5 min and v_signal = 5 mm/min and falls below Darwin's 5-60 min window, and N_wrap uses the no-support control as its reference. Pass 4: either digitise a quantitative time course (e.g. Jaffe & Galston 1968 Fig. or Isnard & Silk 2009 Table) into the JSON and fit tau_thigmo/v_signal to it, or move both entries out of `measure_morphoeval()` into a 'predictions' list so the quick gate does not count them as reference-anchored.
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:1925-1933 and 1955-1963 — the Gerbode soft peak overwinding (0.7171 vs 0.58 turns, +24 %) and the G-fiber bilayer kappa_0 (0.4976 vs 0.65 mm^-1, -23 %) miss their references by about a quarter; v2 misquoted both. Pass 4: revisit `compute_g_fiber_intrinsic_curvature` (L164-L181) bilayer thickness/modulus ratio against Gerbode et al. (2012) Fig. 2 and the overwinding amplitude in `evaluate_gerbode_overwinding_regimes` (L1040-L1088), and report the deviations in the figure.
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:483-514 and 1588-1591 — `_wrap_statistics` counts winding of every distal node about the support axis, so N_wrap = 2.86 with only 33 % of nodes in contact includes loose loops (mean loop radius > R_s + a), yet panel G's title reports "N = 2.9" without the qualifier. Pass 4: report tight wraps (nodes with rho < R_s + a + tol) separately from enclosing loops, add a contact-feedback growth law so kappa0 keeps rising until contact (the JSON `residual_remediation` already proposes this), and label panel G accordingly.
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:596-909 vs 249-411 — the contact-coiling rod is a separate bending-only discrete rod with no material-frame twist, so Gamma = C/B (the quantity that drives Laws 2-3) plays no role in contact coiling and the zero-link perversion physics is never solved together with support contact. Pass 4: add a twist degree of freedom (Cosserat / Bishop-frame twist angle per edge) to the section 3b rod, or drive section 3 `relax_kirchhoff_perversion_rod` with the contact-gated kappa0 and a cylinder constraint, and show that a tethered tendril wrapping a support still forms a perversion.
- remediation needed: 1998-goriely-tendril-perversion-intrinsic-curvature.py:741-761 and 1851-1860 — Coulomb friction uses normal forces lagged one macro step, so F_hold / mu*sum(N) = 0.67 is partly a numerical artefact of the lag plus partial contact; the self-test accepts any value in (0.1, 1.5) (L2044). Pass 4: iterate the normal force to self-consistency within each macro step (or use a semi-smooth Newton / augmented-Lagrangian contact step), then tighten the acceptance band and report the capstan-law comparison exp(mu Theta) as a measurement.
- remediation needed: morphoeval/cloud/dispatches/slot-064.json `slug` ("human-brain-folding-3d") and the pass3 run yaml `paper` field (Tallinen et al. 2016) do not describe this tendril script; both are campaign metadata outside this slot's writable files (`init` sets the run paper). Flagged for the campaign coordinator rather than edited.

At the audit (pass 3, 2026-10-20) the assessor listed these remediation items, quoted:
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:1073-1139 — the 12-species quarter-power regression uses EI, k values that were set from lambda_obs, so r = 1.0000 and alpha = 0.2500 are tautological. Replace with an independent predictor (e.g. measured shell thickness h -> EI ~ E h^3/12 and k from margin curvature) or re-label the panel and measurement as a consistency check, not a validation.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:1289 and 2343, 1265 — `evaluate_repair_outcome_phase_diagram` is called with the default seed only, so `--chip-half-angle` / `--repair-k-ratio` move panel H but not panel I; `--self-test` help still says "8-check" (12 run) and the section banner still says "6-Panel" (3 x 3). Forward the overrides as the grid centre and fix the two stale strings.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:2069-2079, 2119-2129, 2089-2110 — the three Pass 3 headline references (eps_close vs M = 224 convergence, critical chip vs 1.5 lambda rounding heuristic, heal length 8.3 vs imposed 7 mm) are model-internal. Vendor at least one empirical anchor: repair-scar frequency / in-register rate from Vermeij (1987) or a later shell-repair survey, or digitised Murex spine cross-sections.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:224, 371, 473, 516, 651, 758, 1276, 2039 vs datasets/mollusc_shell_marginal_buckling/mollusc_shell_marginal_buckling_reference.json:65, 132-136, 149 — EI = 1.085 mN mm^2 is hard-coded in eight places and is the value that makes lambda_c = 8.7766 mm give exactly 14 ribs over L = 122.87 mm, while the pinned JSON gives default EI = 0.180 and Adult_V EI = 1.79131. Read EI from the JSON (one stage), derive it from mantle thickness and modulus, and report the rib count as a prediction rather than a calibration target.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:234, 263, 328, 834-836 — the margin is periodic on [0, L) (FFT), so a repair-induced extra rib slides the whole 14 -> 15 pattern globally (adult correlation ~ 0 in defect cells of the phase diagram); the rib count also depends on a find_peaks prominence of 0.25 A_eq. Implement a free-edge or auricle-pinned (hinged) margin with a finite-difference or Chebyshev discretisation so defects localise, and report rib counts with a sensitivity to the prominence threshold.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:310, 357, 605, 2289-2300 — L-BFGS-B never meets ftol = 1e-16 / gtol = 1e-13 and always exits at maxiter (600; 500 in the trajectory), which is why self-test #10 needs a 1-2 % of A_eq tolerance. Use realistic tolerances (ftol ~ 1e-12, gtol ~ 1e-8) and assert convergence (`opt.success`) in the self-test, or switch to a Newton-Krylov solve of the Euler-Lagrange equation.
- remediation needed: 2013-chirat-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling.py:511-743 — the hollow-spine closure is a planar inextensible elastica with prescribed W = 6 mm, t = 0.35 mm and penalties mu = 400; no out-of-plane coupling between cross-sections, no shell stretching energy, no growth tensor. Build the 3D finite-strain morphoelastic shell FEM with volumetric growth (Rudraraju et al. 2019) or at least a Kirchhoff-rod / shell-strip model in which W and t emerge from the margin solution, and validate eps_close against a measured Murex spine cross-section rather than mesh convergence of the same model.
- remediation needed: morphoeval/cloud/dispatches/slot-072.json:25 and morphoeval/runs/2026-10-19-mollusc-shell-marginal-buckling-loop-pass3.yaml (run.paper) — slot metadata names `cahn-hilliard-biosilica` / Lenoci & Camp (2008) diatom biosilica / *Thalassiosira pseudonana* for a Chirat/Erlich mollusc-shell script. - remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:163, 213, 677 — two foundation stiffnesses for the same law (K_s = 0.48 for the frond cascade, K_s_eff = 1.98 for comb/Koiter/graded); `--K-s` (L1985) reaches only the frond synthesiser (L1263). Unify on one sourced K_s (or document the effective-vs-material distinction) and thread `--K-s` and `--E` through every solver including the elastica and varix modules; fix the stale "8-check" help text (L1981).
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:1826, 1866, 1773, 1236 — reference values that equal the script's own output or an analytic identity (neck-gap delta -3.1059; specimen CV 0.2092; beta* = 4/3; rigid psi* 22.78 deg). Replace each with an external anchor (e.g. literature spine-spacing CV for Murex pecten, measured neck gaps from Moulton 2015 Fig. 6) or mark `reference_value: null` with `derived_from: model`.
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:1874-1976 — self-test wall time ~65-75 s because the locking and obliquity sweeps run at full resolution; add a reduced-resolution fast path (n_s = 96, n_t = 48 as at L1941) for the sweeps under `--self-test` and keep the full sweeps behind a flag.
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:230-263 — `solve_murex_siphonal_comb` builds the foundation from the rounded mode q_mode = 2 pi round(L/lambda_1)/L (k_sub = q_mode^4, L256) and seeds the 16-mode (L263), so the "L-BFGS-B relaxed spine count 16.0 vs 16.0" measurement (L1812-1820) is prescribed. Replace with the Koiter-style noise initialisation on K_0 = (k_1^*)^4 (as at L670-900) so the count is emergent (theory 16.47), and relabel the measurement; also make `EI_eff`, `P_load`, `kappa_3` dimensional or drop the `_mm` suffixes (L255-260).
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:335-386 and 43-44 — `solve_kirchhoff_elastica_spine_loop` does not integrate the Kirchhoff-Clebsch ODE stated in the header; it draws a parametric omega loop (cos^1.8 profile, L375) with a linear neck gap (L364) and an uncited height law 4.8 sqrt(gamma - gamma_c) (L368, reused at L747). Integrate the elastica with unilateral self-contact (shooting or collocation) and couple its cross-section to the Koiter surface height scale, closing the residual of Pass 2 item 1.
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:411-417 and 457-462 — the Chicoreus frond stages are hand-drawn cosines and the varix cycle prescribes 120 deg Gaussian bursts, so the k_2/k_1 = 3.80 (L1806; h_2 = 0.0708 chosen at L182/L391 to hit it) and the 120.0 deg (L1836) measurements are circular. Derive the secondary serrations by solving the comb energy on the primary frond with h_2, and let varix spacing emerge from a growth-rate / rest-period dynamic (Lean Law 3) instead of a prescribed gamma(phi).
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:497-556 with datasets/mollusc_aperture_spine_buckling/mollusc_aperture_spine_buckling_reference.json:114-150 — `k2_over_k1_obs`, `n_primary_spines_obs`, h_1 and h_2 per species have no measurement source and match the predictions to rounding (r = 1.0000 / 0.9987). Source each row to a published figure/table or relabel the table as model-generated and drop the two cross-taxa correlations from `measure_morphoeval()`.
- remediation needed: 2015-moulton-mollusc-aperture-spine-buckling.py:670-900 — the Koiter surface is linearised on a flat bi-periodic torus with D = 1 (nondimensional) and periodic t with subcritical margins; the free count 17 is quantised by the domain and shifted by onset excess (q_max = sqrt(P/2)); `converged` falls back to a gradient-norm test at maxiter (L817); the height-modulation metric is uninformative for locked patterns. Add reference-surface curvature and finite membrane strain (or a true FE shell per Rudraraju 2019), report D in N mm, test domain-size independence of the free count, and remove or replace the hmod metric.
